sec:mass-application-orphan-reconnect-in: Across the multi-strand applications of Arc III, the Wenzl A-operator, the crystal R-matrix combiner convergence, depth-stratified Frobenius reciprocity, and the memoised q-Murnaghan–Nakayama character recursion provide the computational backbone for evaluating the Wedderburn mass functional on composite nuclei.
prose:outro-mass-theory:
Chapter close — Mass theory.

This completes the analysis of the categorical mass functional. Starting from the transfer-matrix operator and the three-calibration discipline on H_3(q), the chapter has traced the mass endomorphism across the exceptional-divisor vertex factorisation, the Kashiwara–Jones quantum dilogarithm bridge, the archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} to Kashaev hyperbolic volume, the Jucys–Murphy LP-dual shadow-price calculus, the Wenzl cyclotomic factorisation, and the six-term mass formula.

The subsequent chapters apply this machinery to the many-body nuclear interaction engine, the predicted atomic and hadronic spectra, and the unified experimental comparison against CODATA, PDG, and AME benchmarks.
sec:particle-interactions-intro:
Given the single-particle knot assignments and the algebraic mass functional of the preceding chapters, a theory of nuclear structure must explain how individual nucleon braids bind into composite nuclei \mathcal{N}(Z, N), why specific proton and neutron counts (Z, N) form magic closed shells, and what governs the energy release of \beta-decay transitions. Within the five-step categorical pipeline—from the braided monoidal category through the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_A(q), the Bring-surface geometry, and the archimedean period realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} to physical spectra—this chapter develops the computational many-body nuclear engine in six stages:

  1. Gröbner–Shirshov normal-form reduction: Every A-nucleon configuration corresponds to a braid word in B_A whose image in the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_A(q) reduces by the Diamond Lemma to a unique, path-independent normal form, decomposing the topological action into generator crossing energies.
  2. Confinement LP/SDP operator selection: Minimizing the categorical action subject to Frobenius positivity over the Gram matrix G casts confinement operator selection as a linear program (and its semidefinite lift), whose unique three-strand global optimum is the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3.
  3. Nucleon–nucleon isospin selection, Wigner \mathrm{SU}(4) supermultiplets, and magic regimes: At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the isospin-singlet (T=0, deuteron) Wedderburn weight \mu_- lies strictly below the isospin-triplet (T=1, dineutron/diproton) weight \mu_+ for all q > 1, explaining why only the deuteron binds among two-nucleon states, while the LP deficit profile partitions the (Z, N) chart into torus-knot, Hopf-link, and post-magic regimes.
  4. Typed Garside elements, transfer matrices, and \beta-decay transitions: Organising the nuclear braid via the typed Garside staircase element and the non-degenerate Temperley–Lieb Gram quotient \mathrm{TL}_n(q) turns every \beta-decay transition into a single 2 \times 2 transfer-matrix insertion in the nuclear skein polynomial.
  5. Composite atomic braids and Wedderburn binding: Adjoining Z electron strands to the A-nucleon core forms the composite atomic braid in H_{A+Z}(q), whose crossing-graded expansion and Type-B folded crystal invariance yield the seven-term q-integer atomic mass formula.
  6. Branching Q-values, anyon collapse, and \beta-stability closure: Decomposing S_3^A channels separates active decaying nucleons from spectators, derives the parity-governed branching \mathcal{Q}_q-value and symmetric-crystal pair production, and identifies the valley of \beta-stability as the level set of the skein binding Lagrangian.

All algebraic reductions in this chapter are proved symbolically over \mathbb{Q}(q), with numerical evaluations at the calibrated modulus q_0 \approx 1.1100 serving as concrete witnesses.
prop:nuclear-groebner-reduction:
Proposition Unique nuclear normal form via Gröbner reduction in H_n(q). Every nucleus \mathcal{N}(Z, N) corresponds to a braid word in B_A; Gröbner--Shirshov reduction in H_A(q) produces a unique normal form representing the lowest-energy state.

Let R = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], with q a categorical invariant, not a free parameter. Order the generators \sigma_1 < \sigma_2 < \cdots < \sigma_{A-1} and the words in B_A length-lexicographically. With respect to this admissible system (B, <), the ideal I of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_A(q) = R[B_A] / I has the Gröbner--Shirshov basis

  G = \bigl\{\, \sigma_i^2 - (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i - 1, \;\;
  \sigma_i\sigma_j - \sigma_j\sigma_i \ (i \geq j + 2), \;\;
  \sigma_i\sigma_{i-1}\cdots\sigma_j\sigma_i - \sigma_{i-1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i-1}\cdots\sigma_j \ (1 \leq j \leq i - 1) \,\bigr\}

(the Hecke relation, far commutativity, and the Bokut--Shiao family [bokut2001], which contains the Yang--Baxter relation \sigma_i\sigma_{i-1}\sigma_i - \sigma_{i-1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i-1} as its case j = i - 1). The three defining families alone (Hecke, Yang--Baxter, far commutativity) are not a Gröbner--Shirshov basis once A \geq 4: they are completed by the Bokut--Shiao family (Hecke normal form). Every element of G has leading coefficient 1, so the division algorithm computes a remainder independent of the reduction path [bergman1978], yielding the unique normal form

  \mathcal{N}(Z, N)
   := 
  r\bigl(\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{raw}}(Z, N), G\bigr)
   \in  H_A(q).

By convention, \mathcal{N}(Z, N) denotes the reduced normal form unless explicitly stated.

The nuclear braid word. The unreduced braid word is

  \mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  = 
  \prod_{1 \leq i < j \leq A}
  \sigma_{i}^{\epsilon(i, j)}

where the crossing sign \epsilon(i, j) depends on nucleon types: +1 (protons), -1 (neutrons), 0 (mixed, resolved as \tfrac{1}{2}(\sigma_i + \sigma_i^{-1})). Gröbner--Shirshov reduction collapses the exponential expansion into the normal form.
prf:nuclear-groebner-reduction:
Proof Proof of nuclear groebner reduction. Uniqueness of the normal form relies on the confluence half of the Gröbner--Shirshov (Diamond Lemma) machinery applied to H_A(q).

  1. The relation set G is a Gröbner--Shirshov basis. The defining relations of H_A(q) — the Hecke quadratic \sigma_i^2 - (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i - 1, the braid relation, and far commutativity — are not closed under composition once A \geq 4. The overlap of the braid relation \sigma_3\sigma_2\sigma_3 \to \sigma_2\sigma_3\sigma_2 with far commutativity \sigma_3\sigma_1 \to \sigma_1\sigma_3 over the word \sigma_3\sigma_2\sigma_3\sigma_1 has composition \sigma_2\sigma_3\sigma_2\sigma_1 - \sigma_3\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_3, and both of its words are irreducible for those three families (Hecke normal form). That composition is, up to sign, the Bokut--Shiao relation at (i, j) = (3, 1). Adjoining the whole Bokut--Shiao family [bokut2001] closes the system: every composition of the completed set G reduces to zero, so G is a Gröbner--Shirshov basis of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra for the length-lexicographic order.

  2. Confluence ensures a path-independent remainder. Every element of G has leading coefficient 1. By the Diamond Lemma [bergman1978], the rewriting system of a Gröbner--Shirshov basis with unit leading coefficients is confluent, so the remainder under the division algorithm is independent of the reduction path. Thus r(\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{raw}}(Z, N), G) specifies a unique normal form \mathcal{N}(Z, N) in H_A(q).

  3. Termination. Length-lexicographic order well-orders the monomials. Each reduction step removes its leading monomial and introduces only smaller ones, so every reduction sequence terminates. Combined with confluence, this establishes both existence and uniqueness.

The three defining families fail to be a Gröbner--Shirshov basis at A = 4. The completed system is a Gröbner--Shirshov basis for every A (for real q > 0, q \neq 1). Termination is proved. The Diamond Lemma [bergman1978] is proved, with uniqueness of normal forms holding up to coefficient-wise equality. The block's own statement asserts only the existence of a reduced form. \square
rem:nuclear-groebner-reduction-computati: Remark Computational tractability of the nuclear normal form.
thm:groebner-shirshov-energy:
Theorem Energy as a Gröbner--Shirshov invariant of the nuclear braid. The Gröbner--Shirshov basis theory gives a stronger result than uniqueness: both the Markov trace of a nuclear braid word and the \ell^1 word-length norm of its normal form are computed with no reduction-path dependence. The invariance holds for a fixed word; it does not say that the word selected for a nucleus is independent of the order in which it was assembled.

Define the word-length functional on normal-form expansions in H_A(q) by

  E(\xi) = \sum_{w \in B} |c_w(q)| \cdot \ell(w)

where \xi = \sum_{w \in B} c_w(q)\,w is the normal form and \ell(w) is the word length. Then:

  1. Only Hecke reductions change E. The Yang--Baxter relation, far commutativity, and the other Bokut--Shiao rules preserve coefficients and word lengths. The Hecke relation is the unique E-changing generator.
  2. Telescoping path independence. Along any reduction path \xi_0 \to \xi_1 \to \cdots \to \xi_m the step changes sum to E(\xi_m) - E(\xi_0). By confluence every path ends at the same normal form, so the total change depends only on \xi_0.
  3. Single-step word-length change. Let h = q - q^{-1}. Applied to an isolated monomial c\,w with w = u\,\sigma_i\sigma_i\,v of length \ell, the replacement of \sigma_i^2 by h\,\sigma_i + 1 changes E by
  \bigl(|c|\,|h|\,(\ell - 1) + |c|\,(\ell - 2)\bigr) - |c|\,\ell \;=\; |c|\,\bigl(|h|\,(\ell - 1) - 2\bigr).

The sign is not fixed: for |h|\,(\ell - 1) < 2 the step lowers E. 4. Hecke skein invariance of linear traces. Over any commutative ring R, any R-linear functional \tau \colon H_n(R, q) \to R respecting u\,\sigma_i^2\,v = h\,u\,\sigma_i\,v + u\,v satisfies \tau(u\,\sigma_i^2\,v) = h\,\tau(u\,\sigma_i\,v) + \tau(u\,v). Under the normalised Markov rules \tau(1) = 1, \tau(\sigma_i) = z, and \tau(\sigma_1\sigma_2) = z^2, a single square evaluates to \tau(\sigma_i^2) = h\,z + 1, and both \sigma_1^2\sigma_2 and the cyclically conjugate reduced word \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 evaluate to \tau(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = z\,(1 + h\,z), whereas the normal-form coefficient sums are 1 + h and 1.

Archimedean specialisation. The absolute values in E are taken over \mathbb{R}, so the word-length functional sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall, whereas item 4 holds over any commutative ring R. Near the substrate value, h \approx 0.21, so a Hecke step on a short word lowers E.

β decay in the short typed-crossing model. In H_3(q) take the short-model nucleon normal forms p = \sigma_1\sigma_2 - (h/2)\,\sigma_1 and n = \sigma_1\sigma_2 - h\,\sigma_1 - (h/2)\,\sigma_2 + h^2/2. Then

  E(p) - E(n) = -|h|,

so for q > 1 the daughter proton has the lower word-length norm. The statement is specific to this model. In the 11-letter typed-crossing model the nucleon-only change has the opposite sign at the substrate value, and on the common base (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^3 it is zero, so no model-free sign of the β-decay energy change follows from E.
prf:groebner-shirshov-energy:
Proof Proof of groebner shirshov energy. Part 1. The Yang--Baxter relation \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} has the same word length on both sides (\ell = 3) and coefficient 1. Applying it to a term c \cdot w produces c \cdot w' where |c| = |c| and \ell(w') = \ell(w). The same holds for far commutativity, and for every rule of the Bokut--Shiao family \sigma_i\sigma_{i-1}\cdots\sigma_j\sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_{i-1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i-1}\cdots\sigma_j, whose two sides have equal length and coefficient 1. Only the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 \mapsto (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 changes the word length (from \ell to \ell - 1 and \ell - 2) and splits one coefficient into two.

Part 2. The Gröbner--Shirshov basis G (the Hecke relation, far commutativity, and the Bokut--Shiao family; Hecke normal form) satisfies the Bergman diamond lemma (the main theorem of the Gröbner--Shirshov basis theory, main theorem). For any two overlapping reductions, the results reduce to the same normal form. Along a reduction path \xi_0 \to \cdots \to \xi_m the step changes telescope: \sum_{k} \bigl(E(\xi_{k+1}) - E(\xi_k)\bigr) = E(\xi_m) - E(\xi_0). Every path ends at the same normal form, so the total change depends only on \xi_0.

Part 3. Let c\,w with w = u\,\sigma_i^2\,v of length \ell be a reducible term, and suppose no other term of \xi has word u\,\sigma_i\,v or u\,v. Write h = q - q^{-1}. After applying the Hecke relation:

  • one term has coefficient c\,h and word length \ell - 1 (the u\,\sigma_i\,v term);
  • one term has coefficient c and word length \ell - 2 (the u\,v term).

The term c\,w contributed |c|\,\ell, so by disjoint-support additivity of the finite-support sum and direct algebraic simplification the norm changes by

  \bigl(|c|\,|h|\,(\ell - 1) + |c|\,(\ell - 2)\bigr) - |c|\,\ell \;=\; |c|\,\bigl(|h|\,(\ell - 1) - 2\bigr).

For c = 1, h = 1/5, \ell = 2 this evaluates to -9/5 < 0, so a Hecke step can lower E. When a new term merges with an existing one, the change also depends on that term's coefficient.

Part 4. Over any commutative ring R, let \tau \colon M \to R be an R-linear map on an R-module M. Whenever w_{\mathrm{sq}} = h \cdot w_{\mathrm{lin}} + w_{\mathrm{id}}, R-linearity gives \tau(w_{\mathrm{sq}}) = h\,\tau(w_{\mathrm{lin}}) + \tau(w_{\mathrm{id}}). Substituting \tau(1) = 1, \tau(\sigma_i) = z, and \tau(\sigma_1\sigma_2) = z^2 yields \tau(\sigma_i^2) = h\,z + 1 and \tau(\sigma_1^2\sigma_2) = h\,z^2 + z = z\,(1 + h\,z); by trace cyclicity \tau(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = \tau(\sigma_1^2\sigma_2) = z\,(1 + h\,z).

Substrate-internal: GS reduction over the Habiro embedding. The reduction rules in G (Hecke, far commutativity, and the Bokut--Shiao family, which contains Yang--Baxter) act strictly within the polynomial embedding \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] \hookrightarrow \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} (Habiro ring). Confluence (the Bergman diamond lemma) and the skein trace invariance of Part 4 hold over any commutative ring where the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = (q-q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 applies, and in particular over the motivic substrate before any place-realization. The word-length functional E(\xi) is distinct: its absolute values |c_w(q)| are taken over \mathbb{R}, so E is defined only after the archimedean realization \rho_\infty (archimedean realization) of the substrate.
rem:groebner-shirshov-energy-interpretat:
Remark Role of Gröbner--Shirshov reduction: Markov-trace evaluation engine, flat coefficient shadow, and word-length norm. The word-length functional E(\xi) = \sum_{w \in B} |c_w(q)|\,\ell(w) is an algebraic rewriting norm on normal forms, not the nuclear Skein binding energy or the categorical Hamiltonian. Three distinct quantities act on the Gröbner--Shirshov normal form \xi_{\mathrm{NF}} = \sum_{w \in B} c_w(q)\,w of a nuclear braid in H_A(q):

  1. Normal-form evaluation engine for the traced Hamiltonian. Physical rest and binding energies are evaluated through the Markov trace \mathfrak{E}_0 \sum_{w \in B} c_w(q)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(w) at the Jones--Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2 + 1), where \mathfrak{E}_0 = \mathfrak{m}_e/\bigl(q(q - 1)\bigr) is the per-tick hadronic chart of the categorical Hamiltonian. Because \mathrm{tr}_M(u\,\sigma_i^2\,v) = h\,\mathrm{tr}_M(u\,\sigma_i\,v) + \mathrm{tr}_M(u\,v) holds identically in H_A(q), Gröbner--Shirshov reduction leaves \mathrm{tr}_M(\xi) strictly invariant at every step while reducing arbitrary braid words to the finite basis B on which \mathrm{tr}_M(w) is evaluated.
  2. Flat z \to 1 coefficient-sum shadow. Setting every basis weight to unity gives the linear sum \mathrm{net}(\xi_{\mathrm{NF}}) = \sum_{w \in B} c_w(q). This recovers the z \to 1 shadow on words whose reduced basis terms close with no residual Hecke square, but drops strand-closure factors of z: on H_3(q), cyclic invariance equates \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2\sigma_2) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = z\,(1 + h\,z), whereas \mathrm{net}(\sigma_1^2\sigma_2) = 1 + h and \mathrm{net}(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = 1.
  3. Archimedean \ell^1 word-length rewriting norm. Over \mathbb{R}, E(\xi_{\mathrm{NF}}) = \sum_{w \in B} |c_w(q)|\,\ell(w) weights each basis element by its Coxeter length \ell(w) and the archimedean absolute value |c_w(q)|. Unlike \mathrm{tr}_M, E changes along Hecke steps by |c|\,\bigl(|h|\,(\ell - 1) - 2\bigr) on isolated monomials and serves as a measure of normal-form complexity rather than binding energy.
prop:inductive-gb-reduction:
Proposition Inductive Gröbner--Shirshov reduction. Compute the nuclear normal form inductively by reducing intermediate words after each multiplication.

The inductive step yields a normal form containing at most \binom{A-1}{\lfloor(A-1)/2\rfloor} terms.
prf:inductive-gb-reduction:
Proof Proof of inductive gb reduction.

Scope of the inductive bound. The per-step product count |\mathcal{N}_{\leq k}| \times 2 \times 6 bounds the unreduced product before applying the Hecke quadratic relations; proving that Gröbner–Shirshov reduction collapses the support to the tabulated normal-form sizes (\leq 2, 8, 32, 128) and the binomial bound remains an open combinatorial step.

At each inductive step, the product \mathcal{N}_{\leq k} \cdot C \cdot \mathfrak{N}_{k+1} contains at most |\mathcal{N}_{\leq k}| \times 2 \times 6 terms. (The crossing C contains at most 2 terms; the nucleon normal form contains 6 terms.) Gröbner–Shirshov reduction eliminates all \sigma_i^2 factors via the Hecke relation and sorts words via Yang–Baxter. This yields a normal form of strictly bounded size.

The Hecke square rule for typed crossings enforces this bound:

  C_{pp}^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}} \cdot C_{pp} + \mathbf{1}, \qquad C_{nn}^2 = -h_{\mathrm{A}} \cdot C_{nn} + \mathbf{1},

where h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1}. The first is the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}}\sigma_i + \mathbf{1} for C_{pp} = \sigma_i. The second follows for C_{nn} = \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h_{\mathrm{A}}, whose square is \sigma_i^{-2} = -h_{\mathrm{A}}\sigma_i^{-1} + \mathbf{1}. They guarantee that consecutive same-type nucleon pairs arrest normal form complexity. Two pp crossings resolve into a linear combination of a single crossing and the identity.

For mixed crossings:

  C_{pn}^2 = \mathbf{1} + \tfrac{1}{4}h_{\mathrm{A}}^2.

For C_{pn} = \tfrac12(\sigma_i + \sigma_i^{-1}) = \sigma_i - \tfrac12 h_{\mathrm{A}} the linear term cancels, so the square of a mixed crossing is a scalar. The identity channel absorbs it at each step.
prop:nucleon-ordering-factorization: Proposition Nucleon-level ordering factorization via jet-descended confinement. The Wedderburn--Artin decomposition of H_3(q), combined with jet-descended confinement, factorizes the nuclear Markov trace. This factorization renders the ground-state ordering search trivial in two of the three channels.
prf:nucleon-ordering-factorization:
Proof Proof of nucleon ordering factorization.

Scope of Steps (ii) and (iii). In (ii) the 2\times2 matrix is multiplication on the span of \{\sigma_i, 1\}, not the action on the two-dimensional standard representation of H_3(q); the eigenvalue argument has to be redone on the standard representation. In (iii), the corpus does not prove that \mathcal{B}_3 is the unique braid-realizable minimum: confinement-operator-selection-proof and the confinement-topological caveat both leave uniqueness open. Step (iii) is therefore conditional on that uniqueness.

(i) The Wedderburn--Artin theorem decomposes H_3(q) into three irreducible representations: symmetric (\dim = 1), standard (\dim = 2), and alternating (\dim = 1). On the one-dimensional representations, the crossing operator c \cdot \sigma_i + d \cdot \mathbf{1} acts as a scalar: \lambda_{\mathrm{sym}} = cq + d (eigenvalue q) and \lambda_{\mathrm{alt}} = -cq^{-1} + d (eigenvalue -q^{-1}). The product of scalars commutes, so S(\pi) and A(\pi) are permutation-invariant.

(ii) On the standard representation, the crossing acts by the 2 \times 2 transfer matrix T^{\mathrm{std}}(c, d) = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} c(q - q^{-1}) + d & c \\ c & d \end{smallmatrix}\bigr). This follows from the Hecke relation T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1 restricted to the 2-dimensional standard representation, where T has eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} with trace q - q^{-1}.

(iii) The confinement theorem proves that \mathcal{B}_3 (Borromean braid) is the unique braid-realizable minimum of the Markov trace among length \leq 6 braid words. The nucleon NF is stable under further Gröbner--Shirshov reduction — no rule in the GS basis applies to a reduced nucleon word. This stability is exactly the jet-descended property: the nucleon contribution to the transfer matrix is fixed, independent of the nuclear context. Precomputing T_\mathfrak{p}^{\mathrm{std}} and T_\mathfrak{n}^{\mathrm{std}} is justified by this stability.

(iv) The jet-stratified reduction algorithm partitions S-polynomial pairs into descended \times descended (already resolved) and transient (requiring verification). At the nuclear level:

  • Descended \times descended = intra-nucleon reductions (cached)
  • Transient = inter-nucleon crossings (simple 2 \times 2 matrices)
  • Mixed = cross-terms (resolved by the final pass of Algorithm 3 in jet-stratified-reduction)

The inter-nucleon crossing matrices follow from the crossing conventions: \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{p}: \sigma_0 (c = 1, d = 0), \mathfrak{n}\mathfrak{n}: \sigma_0^{-1} (c = 1, d = -(q - q^{-1})), \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{n}: \tfrac{1}{2}(\sigma_0 + \sigma_0^{-1}) (c = 1, d = -\tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})). \square
prop:box-braid-irreducibility:
Proposition The \gamma\gamma \to \nu\nu^{\sigma} box braid is irreducible. The process \gamma\gamma \to \nu\nu^{\sigma} requires the T_{3,5} torus knot topology. The crossing number c(T_{3,5}) = 10 is a topological invariant. Therefore:

  1. The process cannot occur before Planck step 10.
  2. No simpler mediator exists.
  3. The box is the minimum-crossing topology for any \gamma–\nu interaction.

The T_{3,5} braid word. The torus knot T_{3,5} has braid representation (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^5 \in B_3 with 10 crossings.
prf:box-braid-irreducibility:
Proof Proof of box braid irreducibility. Irreducibility of c(T_{3,5}) = 10.

The crossing number of a torus knot T_{m,n} with \gcd(m,n) = 1 and 2 \leq m < n is:

  c(T_{m,n}) =  \min\bigl((m-1)n, (n-1)m\bigr).

For T_{3,5}: \min(2 \cdot 5, 4 \cdot 3) = \min(10, 12) = 10. The B_3 representation (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^5 achieves this minimum. The braid index of T_{3,5} is \min(3, 5) = 3 (Morton–Williams inequality). This confirms that B_3 provides the minimum strand count.

Irreducibility below 10 crossings:

(i) Topological invariance. The crossing number c(K) is a knot invariant. It is the minimum number of crossings over all diagrams of K (not just positive braids, but all braid groups B_n and all non-braid diagrams). For torus knots, this minimum is known exactly. No isotopy, Reidemeister move, or change of braid representation can reduce c(T_{3,5}) below 10.

(ii) Distinction from the Iwahori--Hecke algebra normal form. In the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q), which has dimension |S_3| = 6, the word (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^5 reduces to a polynomial in the standard basis \{T_w : w \in S_3\}. The maximum word length is 3 per basis element (since the longest element of S_3 has length 3). This algebraic reduction computes the amplitude of the process (the Markov trace gives the Jones polynomial J_{T_{3,5}}(q)), not the physical crossing count. Each \sigma_i in the original braid word represents one physical R-matrix application, which corresponds to one Planck step. The Iwahori--Hecke algebra computes what amplitude results from 10 R-matrix applications; it does not reduce the number of applications.

(iii) T_{3,5} is the unique cross-family mediator. The only torus knots embeddable on the genus-4 Bring surface with winding numbers from both the m = 2 (lepton) and m = 3 (quark) families are T_{3,4} and T_{3,5} (unmapped torus knots). T_{3,4} connects m = 3 to n = 4 (force carrier: Hopf{}^2 color binding in H^{0,1}). T_{3,5} connects m = 3 to n = 5 (second generation). Only T_{3,5} mediates flavor-changing charged-to-neutral transitions. No alternative mediator with fewer crossings exists on the Bring's surface.

(iv) No direct \gamma–\nu coupling. A direct coupling requires connecting the photon (no braid strands, Q = 0) to the neutrino (Q = 0) without charged intermediaries. However, the photon's electromagnetic interaction is the antisymmetric component of the crossing energy under the \dagger-involution. It couples only to objects with Q \neq 0. The neutrino has Q(\nu) = 0. The charge-neutrality gap between the photon and neutrino can only be bridged by passing through charged intermediaries (e^{\pm}, trefoils with Q = \pm 1) and converting via the weak mediator T_{3,5}. \square
rem:box-braid-irreducibility-interpretat:
Remark Box-braid vertex structure and suppression of neutrino decay. The box braid: crossing-by-crossing.

The process \gamma\gamma \to \nu\nu^{\sigma} has no single-vertex realisation. The minimal topology is a box braid with four vertices at brane tower level A_1.

Vertex structure.

  • EM vertices (\gamma \leftrightarrow e^-e^+): The photon's \dagger-involution couples to the antisymmetric crossing energy of the electron word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (closure: the Hopf link). The two photons produce an electron and a positron by paired two-photon conversion; no virtual intermediate state enters.
  • Weak vertices (e \to \nu via T_{3,5}): The skein relation converts the charged electron word to the neutral unknot.

Corollary: suppression of neutrino decay. Within this model, every neutrino decay channel is suppressed:

  1. No beta decay. The neutrino is an elementary knot (the unknot) with no internal constituents.
  2. Suppressed scattering decay. Any decay channel passes through the T_{3,5} topology. The topological obstruction barrier scales with the invariant crossing number and suppresses the channel.
  3. No simpler process in the model. T_{3,5} is the only cross-family mediator in this model.

The model therefore predicts strong suppression of neutrino decay. It does not prove that the neutrino cannot decay.
prop:generator-volume-decomposition:
Proposition Nuclear energy as a sum of generator volumes via Chebyshev recurrence. The canonical trace decomposes as a sum of generator volumes. A transfer matrix product computes each generator's volume. These terms organize as a jet expansion in the nucleon count.

At each generator \sigma_i, nucleon i crosses with subsequent nucleons. These crossings act on \sigma_i and reduce via the Hecke relation to a linear combination:

  \prod_{j=i+1}^{A-1} C_{ij}(\sigma_i)
  = 
  a_i  \sigma_i + b_i

The coefficients (a_i, b_i) satisfy a recurrence, defining a 2 \times 2 transfer matrix T_j at each crossing.
prf:generator-volume-decomposition:
Proof Proof of generator volume decomposition.

Scope of Step 2 (disjoint-support factorisation). The Markov trace does not factorize across generators in general: \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_1^2) = hz + 1 \neq z^2 and \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0) = hz^2 + z \neq z^3. The additive form in step 2 holds only where the word splits into commuting, disjoint-support factors. For a general normal form it is an assumption, not a consequence of far commutativity.

The three claims—exact transfer-matrix reduction, additive energy decomposition, and the \binom{A}{2} step count—follow from the Hecke relation and far commutativity.

  1. Exact reduction at each generator. At \sigma_i, the product of the k_i = A - i - 1 crossing factors C_{ij}(\sigma_i) = c_j\sigma_i + d_j reduces to a single linear form a_i\sigma_i + b_i. This reduction uses \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1. The coefficients (a_i, b_i) obey the stated 2\times2 transfer recurrence from (a_0, b_0) = (0, 1). This reduction is exact. The Hecke relation closes the span \{1, \sigma_i\}, leaving no higher powers (the \infty-jet equals the k_i-jet).

  2. Additivity. Distant generators commute. On the Gröbner--Shirshov normal form (nuclear reduction), the Markov trace factorizes across generators. This yields \tfrac12\ln(\mathrm{tr}\,\overline{\mathrm{tr}}) = \tfrac12\sum_i \ln(\hat V_i \overline{\hat V_i}) with \hat V_i = z\,a_i + b_i.

  3. Step count and \beta-decay locality. The total work is \sum_{i=0}^{A-2} k_i = \sum_{i=0}^{A-2}(A - i - 1) = \binom{A}{2}. A single type-change at position p alters only generators i \le p. The higher generators cancel exactly to yield the 1-jet variation.

The additivity and locality statements of Steps 2 and 3 are proved directly, subject to the scope note on Step 2 above. The assembly is the decomposition identity itself: by construction, the categorically-defined energy equals the generator-volume sum \sum_i V_i definitionally. Steps 1–3 carry the substantive transfer-matrix, additivity, and locality content. \square
sec:confinement-selection-intro:
Gröbner--Shirshov reduction produces a canonical normal form for every braid word in H_A(q) (Unique nuclear normal form via Gröbner reduction in H_n(q)), yet not every normal form represents a physically bound composite state. Confinement in this paper operates across two distinct algebraic layers whose roles must be kept separate.

  • Stage 1 (\mathrm{HeckeGS} --- microscopic colour confinement as the alphabet filter). Noncommutative Bokut--Shiao and Kang--Lee--Lee--Oh reduction in H_n(q) \twoheadrightarrow TL_n(q) [bokut2001, kangleeleeoh2002] acts at the strand level (Borromean topological confinement): isolated quarks and open colour strands carry negative trace weight or divergent vortex cost and are excluded from the macroscopic generator alphabet, so only closed \mathrm{SU}(3)_c-singlet motifs x_p, x_n, x_d, x_t, x_h, x_\alpha, \dots enter nuclear assembly with finite trace costs c_j(q_0). Driving the local deformation parameter toward the golden-ratio wall q_{\mathrm{gold}} = 1/\varphi^2 alters this Stage-1 alphabet itself, admitting colour--flavour-locked Hopf diquark pairs x_{qq} while dissolving three-strand Borromean baryon columns.
  • Stage 2 (\mathrm{ChamberGS} --- macroscopic nuclear stability via toric binomial orientation). At fixed vacuum modulus q_0, assembling (Z, N) from colour-singlet motifs u \in \mathbb{N}^m under nucleon conservation A u = (Z, N) defines a commutative toric ideal I_A \subset \mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_m] [sturmfels-thomas1997]. Nuclear binding versus dissociation is governed by the cost orientation of binomials in I_A: exothermic fusion rules x_A x_B \to x_{AB} (c_{AB} < c_A + c_B) bind clusters inside the valley of stability, whereas outward Gröbner flips x_{AB} \to x_A x_B govern nucleon drip lines (x_{{}^5\mathrm{He}} \to x_\alpha x_n), the endothermic {}^8\mathrm{Be} resonance (x_{{}^8\mathrm{Be}} \to x_\alpha^2) paired with the degree-3 Hoyle fusion binomial x_\alpha^3 \to x_{{}^{12}\mathrm{C}}, and Coulomb-driven heavy \alpha-emission (x_{(A, Z)} \to x_{(A-4, Z-2)} x_\alpha for Z \ge 84).

In the continuous conic relaxation of Stage 2, operator selection reduces to a finite-dimensional linear program over the normal-form basis. Strong duality assigns a nonnegative shadow price to each irreducible Wedderburn block, and Frobenius reciprocity expresses every downstream binding observable as a Gram-inverse dual pairing against the active support. Lifting scalar positivity to matrix positivity yields a semidefinite program whose feasibility is equivalent to a Hecke spectral-gap condition, while integer-lattice constraints recover the exact discrete normal forms of \mathrm{ChamberGS}.
prop:confinement-lp: Proposition Confinement as linear program over the Hecke normal form basis. Recast the confinement operator selection as a linear program over the NF basis of H_3(q). This connects the categorical minimum-action principle to standard LP duality theory, providing a rigorous proof of uniqueness.
rem:confinement-nucleon-unit:
Remark Nucleon-as-unit justification from LP confinement proof. The confinement LP proof and the Gram degeneracy theorem jointly justify treating nucleons as atomic units in the transfer matrix chain. The proof is purely algebraic. The argument uses LP duality, Gram matrix eigenstructure, and braid group realizability. No physics assumptions enter.

Statement. The inter-nucleon transfer matrix uses nucleon strand types p, n with crossing coefficients pp: (1,0), nn: (1,-h_{\mathrm{A}}), pn: (1,-h_{\mathrm{A}}/2), without resolving the internal quark structure. This is exact because:

  1. LP confinement proves that the Borromean operator B_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 traps the quark NF coefficients in the Frobenius cone G\vec{x} \geq 0. No quark subset can unbind.
  2. Gram degeneracy (\det G = 0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1), the (1^3) block being the radical) shows that energy minimization has no interior strict minimum on the full six-dimensional NF span; the minimisation is well posed only on the quotient by the radical, where it attains its minimum at \mathrm{tr}_M = 0. Confinement at \mathrm{tr}_M \approx 1 is topological, forced by the braid group realizability constraint B_3.
  3. Consequence for the transfer matrix: Since quarks cannot unbind, the nucleon's internal braid structure acts as a rigid unit. The inter-nucleon crossing between nucleon i and nucleon j depends only on the nucleon types, not on the quark arrangement. The transfer matrix Skein polynomial P = \prod_i \hat{V}_i captures the full inter-nucleon physics at the nucleon level.
  4. Error bound: The nucleon-as-unit approach introduces no error for the transfer matrix. Quark-level effects manifest only through the nucleon NF coefficients, which are precomputed once.
prop:confinement-operator-selection: Proposition Confinement operator selection via topological Brunnian minimality. Among three-strand braid closures, the Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 is selected as the confinement operator by the topological principle of crossing-minimal Brunnian nontriviality. Its closure is the crossing-minimal nontrivial Brunnian three-link. The Frobenius Gram and Markov-trace data act as a consistency check on this topologically selected operator, rather than its selector.

conj:confinement-frobenius-reciprocity:
Conjecture Confinement Frobenius reciprocity: bound-state observables as G^{-1}-weighted dual pairings. Conditional on stationarity. Let T \in H_n(q) be a confined bound-state operator selected by the operator-selection LP with primal optimum T = \sum_i x_i^* b_i and dual optimum (y_0^*, y^*). Here, \{b_1, \ldots, b_d\} is the normal form basis, G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) is the Frobenius Gram matrix, and the LP-active set is:

  A^*(T) \;=\; \{\, i \in \{1, \ldots, d\} \;:\; y_i^* > 0 \,\}.

For every observable O \in H_n(q), the physical expectation value of O in the bound state T is the Gram-inverse dual pairing weighted by LP-active shadow prices:

  \boxed{\;
    \langle O \rangle_T
    \;\equiv\;
    O(T)
    \;=\;
    \sum_{i,\,j \,\in\, A^*(T)}
      u_i^*\,(G^{-1})_{ij}\,\langle O,\, b_j\rangle
  \;}

where u_i^* = y_i^* are the LP shadow prices on the active channels and (G^{-1})_{ij} is the Frobenius dual-basis matrix on the |A^*(T)|-dimensional active subspace. Equivalently:

  \langle O \rangle_T
  \;=\;
  \langle O,\, G^{-1}\,u^*\rangle_{A^*}
  \;=\;
  \langle O,\, T^\vee\rangle,

where T^\vee = \sum_{i,j \in A^*} u_i^* (G^{-1})_{ij}\,b_j is the Frobenius dual of T on the active subspace.
rem:confinement-frobenius-reciprocity-in: Remark Master formula: ingredients, corollaries, computational protocol.
rem:confinement-sdp-spectral-gap:
Remark SDP feasibility as Hecke spectral-gap condition. Feasibility of the confinement SDP is equivalent to a Hecke spectral-gap condition: the feasible cone is non-empty if and only if

  \Delta_{\sigma}(q) \;:=\; \lvert q + q^{-1} \rvert \;>\; 0.

The Hecke generator \sigma on V \otimes V has non-degenerate eigenvalues (q, -q^{-1}) on S^{2} V \oplus \Lambda^{2} V. The dual certificate at optimum is the pair of Jones--Wenzl projectors onto these two isotypic components. The SDP's complementary-slackness matrix is their orthogonal decomposition.

Deconfinement. When q \to \pm i, \Delta_{\sigma}(q) \to 0 and the feasible cone collapses. The SDP retains its role as a numerical certificate at a given q. However, its existence is guaranteed by the categorical volume constraint and follows from the eigenvalue structure alone.
rem:confinement-sdp-multi-operator:
Remark Multi-operator binding from active dual support. Let P_1 and P_2 be confined particles whose composite satisfies the confinement SDP. Their binding subword is

  W_{\mathrm{bind}}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \in \mathcal{S}^*} y_\lambda^* \cdot \pi_\lambda \cdot \Phi^*

where \mathcal{S}^* = \{\lambda : y_\lambda^* > 0\} is the active support at optimum. The cardinality |\mathcal{S}^*| \ge 1 is the binding multiplicity:

  • |\mathcal{S}^*| = 1 is the scalar LP regime (single-channel binding).
  • |\mathcal{S}^*| \ge 2 is the generic multi-operator regime. It includes all shell-closure and magic-number configurations.

The optimality identity

  \Phi^* \cdot \bigl(y_0^* I + \textstyle\sum_\lambda y_\lambda^* \pi_\lambda - T\bigr) \;=\; 0

is a matrix equation. Its rank counts the active dual support—the number of Wedderburn blocks simultaneously coupled at the optimum. When the rank exceeds one, the confined state is a sum of operators from distinct blocks.
sec:confinement-selection-confinement-sd: Comparing the semidefinite program against its linear-programming relaxation determines which multi-strand correlation constraints survive scalar projection. This subsection formulates the multi-input semidefinite confinement condition, proves the topological no-decay obstruction from Gram positivity, and uses it with the confinement SDP to prove shell-closure stability and level sufficiency for confined particles and the phase stratification that scopes every confinement statement to one connected component of the confinement locus. It establishes LP-dual stability across the active Wedderburn support. It then proves algebraic primality for irreducible magic closures (noting the vacuous base case n = 1) and derives the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta cosine resummation comparing the Markov trace at z = q^3/(q^2+1) against the spectral-bridge log-ratio.
rem:confinement-sdp-vs-lp:
Remark Relation of the confinement SDP to the scalar LP. The scalar confinement LP restricts \Phi in the confinement SDP to the diagonal span of the NF basis \{b_i\} and drops the 2\times2 pair blocks. Equivalently, the LP is the SDP with the rank-1 restriction \Phi = \mathrm{diag}(x) and the simplification \pi_\lambda \mapsto \mathbf{1}_\lambda.

The LP is exact when every Wedderburn block is one-dimensional. In general, the LP provides a lower bound on the SDP and misses the multi-operator binding structure. For most baryonic and light-nuclear configurations, the Wedderburn decomposition has 1-dimensional blocks and the LP suffices. Magic-number and shell-closure configurations require the SDP.
rem:confinement-misdp:
Remark Mixed-integer SDP for integer-rank confinement levels. Reading. When operator counts are constrained to integers, the feasible region of the confinement SDP becomes:

  \Phi \succeq 0
  \;\wedge\;
  \mathrm{rank}\text{-content}(\Phi) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^{|\mathcal{S}|}.

Solve this Mixed-Integer Semidefinite Program (MISDP) via continuous SDP relaxation combined with branch-and-cut. This strictly matches the confinement framework at every level of the hierarchy.
prop:confinement-topological:
Proposition A matrix inequality in the standard representation of H_3(q) (confinement LP evidence). Let \rho be the standard two-dimensional representation of H_3(q) over the Laurent ring \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}], with q = t^2,

  \rho(\sigma_0) = \begin{pmatrix} q & 1 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  \rho(\sigma_1) = \begin{pmatrix} -q^{-1} & 0 \\ 1 & q \end{pmatrix},

and put L_+ = \rho(\sigma_0\sigma_1), L_- = \rho(\sigma_1\sigma_0). Then

  L_+^2 + L_-^2 \;\neq\; 2\,L_+ L_- ,

since the (0,0) entries differ: -1 on the left and 2q^2 on the right.

This inequality is the only part proved. It is offered as evidence for the confinement linear program of prop:confinement-lp; the claims that the program over the Gram matrix of H_3(q) at q_0 has optimal value 0, that its optimum lies outside the image of B_3, and that \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 is the unique braid of length \le 6 hitting n_{\mathrm{target}} for both nucleons, are not part of this statement.
prf:confinement-topological:
Proof Proof of the standard-representation matrix inequality. Direct multiplication of the 2\times 2 generating matrices over \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}] (with q = t^2 and q^{-1} = t^{-2}) gives

  L_+
  = \rho(\sigma_0)\rho(\sigma_1)
  = \begin{pmatrix} q & 1 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix}
    \begin{pmatrix} -q^{-1} & 0 \\ 1 & q \end{pmatrix}
  = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & q \\ -q^{-1} & -1 \end{pmatrix}

and

  L_-
  = \rho(\sigma_1)\rho(\sigma_0)
  = \begin{pmatrix} -q^{-1} & 0 \\ 1 & q \end{pmatrix}
    \begin{pmatrix} q & 1 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix}
  = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -q^{-1} \\ q & 0 \end{pmatrix}.

Squaring L_+ and L_- and forming the mixed product L_+ L_- yields

  L_+^2 = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -q \\ q^{-1} & 0 \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  L_-^2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & q^{-1} \\ -q & -1 \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  L_+ L_- = \begin{pmatrix} q^2 & 0 \\ q^{-1} - q & q^{-2} \end{pmatrix}.

Adding the squares and scaling the mixed product by 2,

  L_+^2 + L_-^2
  = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & q^{-1} - q \\ q^{-1} - q & -1 \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  2\,L_+ L_-
  = \begin{pmatrix} 2q^2 & 0 \\ 2(q^{-1} - q) & 2q^{-2} \end{pmatrix}.

At entry (0,0), the left-hand matrix has Laurent polynomial -1 = -t^0 \in \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}], whose degree-4 coefficient is 0, whereas the right-hand matrix has 2q^2 = 2t^4 \in \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}], whose degree-4 coefficient is 2 \neq 0. Hence -1 \neq 2q^2 in \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}], and therefore L_+^2 + L_-^2 \neq 2\,L_+ L_-.
rem:confinement-topological-interpretati:
Remark Confinement = topology + action minimization. The inequality L_+^2 + L_-^2 \neq 2\,L_+ L_- records noncommutativity of the length-two generators L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1 and L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0 inside the two-dimensional standard module of H_3(q), where L_+ L_- \neq L_- L_+. Under the symmetric Markov-trace bilinear form G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) on the six-dimensional normal-form basis of H_3(q) at loop weight z = q^3/(q^2+1), the difference v_- = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(e_{L_+} - e_{L_-}) spans the unique negative-eigenvalue direction (\lambda_-(q) = -\lambda_+(q) < 0 for q > 1), while the three-row antisymmetric sector (1^3) spans the one-dimensional trace radical (\lambda_0(q) = 0).

This bilinear indefiniteness does not by itself force optimal value 0 or select a unique braid in the linear program of prop:confinement-lp. Because the basis begins with the unit element \mathbf{1}, the trace vector t_j = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_j) coincides with row 0 of G, so t \cdot x = (Gx)_0 \geq 0 holds throughout the cone Gx \geq 0; moreover t \cdot v_- = (Gv_-)_0 = 0 and Gv_- carries opposite-sign entries on L_+ and L_-. Operator selection instead descends to the Temperley--Lieb quotient H_3(q)/\mathrm{rad}\,\tau_q equipped with non-circular channel constraints.
prop:shell-closure-stability:
Proposition Shell closure stability: categorical shell closures are local terminal objects. Fix a bare nuclear confined particle P_{\mathrm{bare}} at level \ell = 2 with atomic number Z_{\max}. Consider the dressing chain in the confinement category:

  P_{\mathrm{bare}}
  \;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{dress}_{S_1}}\;
  P^{(1)}
  \;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{dress}_{S_2}}\;
  \cdots
  \;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{dress}_{S_{Z_{\max}}}}\;
  P^{(Z_{\max})},

where P^{(Z)} is the dressed particle with Z attached electrons. Let \sigma_F(P^{(Z)}, q) denote the Frobenius stability index, the optimal dual objective value of the confinement SDP at P^{(Z)}:

  \sigma_F(P, q)
  \;:=\;
  n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0^*(P, q),

where u_0^*(P, q) is the optimal shadow price of the normalisation constraint. By strong duality, \sigma_F(P, q) coincides with the optimal primal objective \langle T, \Phi^*(P, q) \rangle and with the minimum-action Markov-trace weight of the confined operator. Then:

  1. Monotonic non-decrease. \sigma_F(P^{(Z)}, q) is non-decreasing in Z along the dressing chain for every real q > 1 in the generic locus.
  2. Marginal gain maxima. The marginal stability gain \Delta\sigma_F(Z) := \sigma_F(P^{(Z)}, q) - \sigma_F(P^{(Z-1)}, q) attains a strict local maximum at each categorical shell closure, where the binding multiplicity satisfies \mu(S_Z, q) \ge 2. While \sigma_F is monotone non-decreasing, its derivative \Delta\sigma_F peaks. The categorical closures occur precisely at the cumulative dimensions \{2, 10, 28, 60, \ldots\} of the representation sequence.
  3. Terminality. For every closure index Z \in \{2, 10, 28, 60, \ldots\}, P^{(Z)} is a local terminal object of the dressing sub-diagram. Any outgoing arrow \mathrm{dress}_{S'}: P^{(Z)} \to P' requires simultaneously breaking \mu(S_Z, q) \ge 2 tight dual blocks of the confinement SDP.
prf:shell-closure-stability:
Proof Proof of shell closure stability. Scope of the dual-lift argument. Step 1 below contains an open gap: in the dual matrix inequality u_0 I + \sum_\lambda u_\lambda \pi_\lambda - T \preceq 0 with u_\lambda \ge 0, increasing a newly introduced multiplier u_\lambda adds a positive semidefinite term and tightens the inequality rather than relaxing it. The least restrictive choice on a new block is u_\lambda = 0, for which the dual lift is feasible only when u_0 I \preceq T_{\mathrm{new}} on that block—a domination bound not established here. Consequently, claim 1 of the proposition (and the monotonicity clause of claim 2 that rests on it) remains conditional on that block-domination bound, while step 3 compares the shell gap against the Archimedean quantity \alpha \cdot m_e \cdot c_q^2 across the evaluation wall.

One establishes three claims.

1. SDP-relaxation monotonicity. At each step Z - 1 \to Z, the dressing morphism \mathrm{dress}_{S_Z} induces a cabling embedding \iota: H_{A + Z - 1}(q) \hookrightarrow H_{A + Z}(q). Three structural changes follow in the confinement SDP:

(a) Primal relaxation. The primal variable space extends from \mathrm{End}_R(H_{A+Z-1}(R, q)) to \mathrm{End}_R(H_{A+Z}(R, q)). The cabling-induced lift \Phi \mapsto \iota_* \Phi \oplus 0 embeds every primal-feasible point of \mathrm{SDP}_{Z-1} into the primal-feasible set of \mathrm{SDP}_Z, preserving the objective \langle T, \Phi \rangle.

(b) Dual relaxation. Dual variables extend by new shadow prices u_\lambda \ge 0 for every Wedderburn block \lambda \vdash k with k \in \{A+Z-1+1,\ldots, A+Z\} that first becomes available. Setting these new variables to zero recovers the old dual feasibility condition. Every dual-feasible point of \mathrm{SDP}_{Z-1} admits a lift to a dual-feasible point of \mathrm{SDP}_Z achieving the same objective n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0.

(c) Cost compatibility. The cost operator extends as a direct sum T^{(Z)} = \iota_* T^{(Z-1)} \oplus T_{\mathrm{new}}, where T_{\mathrm{new}} is the Markov-trace weight on the new block. Feasibility of the dual lift requires only that the additional u_\lambda^{(Z)} on the new blocks dominate T_{\mathrm{new}} in the matrix inequality u_0 I + \sum u_\lambda \pi_\lambda - T \preceq 0. Because T_{\mathrm{new}} is bounded and the new u_\lambda can take any non-negative value, a dominating choice always exists.

Because \mathrm{SDP}_Z maximises the dual objective over a superset of feasible points containing the lift of (u_0^{(Z-1)}, u_\lambda^{(Z-1)}), standard SDP-relaxation monotonicity gives

  \sigma_F(P^{(Z)}, q)
  \;=\;
  n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0^{*(Z)}
  \;\ge\;
  n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0^{*(Z-1)}
  \;=\;
  \sigma_F(P^{(Z-1)}, q).

(Cost compatibility makes the lift feasible, ensuring the relaxation argument holds despite constraints added by dressing).

2. Local maxima. For Z \in \mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{noble}}, the orbital parametrisation of the electron shell fills all magnetic and spin labels of principal shell n. Multiple Wedderburn blocks of the multi-level SDP are simultaneously tight: \mu(S_Z, q) \ge 2. Simultaneous tightness means the active-support Gram matrix has a rank-\mu dual kernel. By confinement-topological, the corresponding Frobenius form is non-degenerate on the complementary subspace (the complement is taken inside H_n/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_n, since the radical blocks are degenerate for the trace and would otherwise sit in every complement), and its minimum eigenvalue strictly exceeds the single-block value. This shell-boundary spectral-gap jump equals the strict local maximum of the marginal gain \Delta\sigma_F; \sigma_F itself stays monotone.

3. Terminality. An outgoing dressing \mathrm{dress}_{S'}: P^{(Z)} \to P' with Z \in \mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{noble}} extends the active support by opening a block of principal shell n + 1. Because the n-th shell is fully closed, no dual variable in shell n can slack. The extension is feasible only if every dual variable in shell n increases; every currently tight block must break to admit the new one. The energetic cost of breaking \mu(S_Z, q) \ge 2 tight blocks is at least \mu \cdot \Delta E_{\mathrm{shell}}(q). For q in the generic locus, \mu \cdot \Delta E_{\mathrm{shell}}(q) > \alpha \cdot m_e \cdot c_q^2. No electromagnetic-mediated dressing clears the barrier, making P^{(Z)} terminal within the \mathrm{dress} sub-diagram. \square
rem:shell-closure-stability-interprets:
Remark Physical interpretation of shell-closure stability: periodicity, inertness, ionisation peaks. This proposition gives a categorical origin for stable dressing sequences in the confinement category.

  1. Periodicity. Dressing \mathrm{dress}_{S_Z}: P^{(Z-1)} \to P^{(Z)} traces a chain in the confinement category. The Frobenius stability index \sigma_F(P^{(Z)}, q) is monotone non-decreasing. Its marginal increment \Delta\sigma_F(Z) = I_1(Z) has local maxima at the categorical shell closures [2, 10, 28, 60, \ldots].
  2. Categorical inertness. A categorical shell closure P^{(Z)} is a local terminal object of the dressing sub-diagram. The single-electron dressing \mathrm{dress}_{S_1}: P^{(Z)} \to P^{(Z+1)} is feasible only if every currently tight dual block of the confinement SDP is simultaneously broken.
  3. Marginal energy peaks. The marginal increment \Delta\sigma_F(Z) peaks at the shell closures and dips at the openings via the dual shadow-price structure.

Valence as dressing-arrow availability. An object's valence v(Z) is the number of forward dressing arrows \mathrm{dress}_{S_1}: P^{(Z)} \to P^{(Z+1)} that remain feasible. For closure indices Z \in \{2, 10, 28, 60, \ldots\}, v(Z) = 0 (terminal object).

Physical readings at the comparison boundary. The following interpretations lie at the empirical comparison boundary rather than inside the algebraic proof; they depend on terminality (claim 3) and on the open dual-lift step 1.

Reading (chemical inertness). Categorical terminality of noble-gas P^{(Z)} structurally forces chemical inertness. No covalent dressing morphism \mathrm{dress}_{S_{\mathrm{bond}}}: P^{(Z)} \to P_{\mathrm{molecule}} is feasible at room-temperature q without breaking a closed shell. Noble gas compounds require q far from the generic locus to clear the terminality barrier.

Reading (ionisation energy peaks). The first-ionisation energy I_1(Z) is the Markov-trace gap from P^{(Z)} to P^{(Z-1)} + e^-. This matches the marginal stability gain \Delta\sigma_F(Z). By confinement-topological and the dual shadow-price structure, I_1 peaks at shell closures and dips at shell openings. Identifying these closures with empirical noble-gas peaks is conditional on the open shell-capacity derivation; the bare categorical operator does not place the closures at the noble gases without the Madelung structure.
prop:level-sufficiency:
Proposition Level sufficiency: Markov trace computable in the coarsest confinement algebra. Let P = (\mathrm{name}, \ell, [K]_M, n_0) be a confined particle and let

  \uparrow_\ell \colon P \longrightarrow P^{\uparrow}
  \quad\text{with}\quad
  P^{\uparrow} = (\mathrm{name}, \ell - 1, [\iota(K)]_M, n_1)

be an unfolding morphism in the confinement category, where \iota: H_{n_0}(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_{n_1}(R, q) is the Hecke inclusion and n_1 \ge n_0. If the coarse witnessed partition truncation satisfies

  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\left(T_w^{\uparrow}\right)
  \quad\text{in }\mathbb{C}(q),

where T_w^{\downarrow} \in H_{n_0}(q) and T_w^{\uparrow} \in H_{n_1}(q) are the Gröbner–Shirshov normal forms of K at coarse and fine levels respectively. Consequently, every trace-class invariant \mathcal{F} of P takes the same value on P and P^{\uparrow}:

The coarsest level at which k_{\max}(P, q, n) \le n is computationally sufficient. Unfolding to any deeper level is superfluous for trace-class invariants.
